sol.section: §§4.5, 4.7, 5.3, 5.6, 6.2, 14.2; reference-interpreter/src/borrow.rs::Facts::sequence, Facts::reversible, Facts::forget_inverses, Node::adjoint and Compiler::compile opaque lowering
sol.problem:
Matched opaque computation/adjoint pairs permanently erase the enclosing saved quantum fact. Use a memoryless ptr_width=32 object, symbol 0 @o and symbol 1 @a, functions in that order, LF after every line. @o signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[1],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":1,"tier":"q"}. @a signature: {"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Exact functions:
oracle @o (p:wire in) (v:wire) (fr:wire[4]) () ()
^entry():
lift.retval p
action @a (t:wire mut) () () (tk:token) ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
f = qalloc any 4
h c
oracle_call @o tk (c) t f () ()
oracle_call @o tk (c) t f () ()
h c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree f
qfree c

Independent §9.2 interface=closure hashes: @o a8f4a15663aead9ecb6618fe3847deba546cf3172f645ffc7e763f551e529e27; @a 4cabd490b0d1a8dfe31489ec234e91867e66b54c6c4d030eb4e8d1cf6f84bb38. With these stored hashes and the standard header/section formatting used by tests/support::object, object_hash is ef010633dbc984abbaa9fbfb97c6233c5390fa99a17bc38e09725cddec936832. hash/check, run-action a --mut 0 --arg token:1,0,0,0, independently started --mut 1 --adjoint with the same token, and reverse with --state "0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8" all actually exit 1, empty stdout, "§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean". Hand: under B=1, @o returns p in one row with code 0, so each call is CX(c,t) and leaves f=0; the two calls are identity, H H restores c=0, and CX(0,b) is identity for arbitrary b and external reference R. The entire action is I_t tensor I_bR. Under B=0, both fault-code XORs also cancel and the same identity holds. Removing only the three borrow/CX/return lines makes check and execution pass, confirming that the ordinary §6 cleanup accepts this matched sequence. The pair inside qloop 2 also rejects.
The same hole affects explicit qinplace inverses. Keep @o/signatures and replace @a by:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () (tk:token) ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
h c
qinplace @o @o tk c
qinplace @o @o tk c
h c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree c
Its independent @a H is bc6e5d89276a62eec7074a716d8dbce40e94a2c80c287ad8fc5b5e5c6c756fbf and stored-H object_hash is 77664ac9392aec50b0415027771ae7ef49dcea7762b70025f0cd918d53a6ee1e. At token B=1, @o is the fault-free identity permutation, both qinplace calls satisfy §4.5, and their matched pair is identity even for a general valid g/ginv pair. check and run-action again actually reject with the same §5.6 diagnostic; deleting the borrow lines makes both pass. In Facts::sequence only Flip/Swap enter reversible(); Opaque calls forget_inverses on all inputs/outputs/controls before Evaluation::apply. Thus even though oracle XOR applications cancel, the initial H record has already gone. qinplace also lacks a canonical inverse-pair identity usable by this history. This is not a function-specific opaque identity needing a claim: oracle self-inversion and the qinplace adjoint are explicit ISA operations.
sol.fix:
Change reference-interpreter/src/borrow.rs::Facts::sequence/reversible and the Node::Opaque inverse representation/lowering (Node::adjoint, Compiler::compile) so matched opaque operations participate in the same causal operation stacks as primitive permutations. Supply an explicit inverse identity: oracle_call is self-adjoint; qinplace swaps @g and @ginv. The key must retain callee(s), token/classical specialisation, actual input/memory/output wires and effective controls. Push the operation on every read/control/output operand above an existing quantum history, and restore the saved expressions only when its matching inverse is on top of all those operand histories. Preserve invalidation for genuinely unmatched opaque readers and lifetime barriers; do not simply keep an H record across an opaque read. Preserve physical frame boundaries, the complete borrowed-touch guard, every return obligation and runtime §4.5 checks.
The determining text is §4.7 "adj oracle_call … ≡ oracle_call …"; §5.3 "reverse order, instruction replaced, versions renumbered" and "qinplace @g @ginv ↦ qinplace @ginv @g   oracle_call ↦ oracle_call"; §6.2 "`other` values are released only by the adjoint of the sequence that produced them"; §14.2 "`qalloc` tensors |0⟩"; and §5.6 "identity on every borrowed bundle and on any external system entangled with it". These determine c=0 at the borrow and I_t tensor I_bR, without a certificate or a new SPEC-QUESTIONS reading.
Add r9_opaque_adjoint_restores_borrow_control in tests/r1_borrow.rs using support::object with the exact two functions/signatures above. Its Object::parse success assertion fails now. After the fix require parse/check/hash success with the independent pins. Allocate t,b,R, bind t as the sole mut and b as the one-wire borrow pool, and supply tk=Argument::Token(Budget::steps(1)). For all eight t/b/R basis inputs, a superposition and a Bell pair between b and R, independently initialise forward and adjoint runs and require exact equality to the entry, no escaping workspace, and exact equality after the opposite direction. Repeat the oracle-pair case with Budget::steps(0). Add the qinplace subject at Budget::steps(1); Budget::steps(0) for qinplace must still reject §4.5 before mutation.
Add pinned counterparts to tests/cli_xam.rs: --mut 0 gives state {"0":[1,0]}, --mut 1 gives {"1":[1,0]}, and --state "0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8" is unchanged, for standalone forward and adjoint. Require wires=1 and reverse equals_entry=true. Extend the deterministic family to qloop 2 around the oracle pair, local child-call wrappers and interleaved histories on separate operands. Retain a negative where only the first oracle call precedes H; borrow/CX/return, with its inverse cleanup after that return: it must still reject even though the final whole-region operation is identity. Rerun the unchanged normal suite and retained certificate/quantum-touch negatives.

codex.problem:
Matched opaque oracle pairs still destroy an outer clean fact. Use a memoryless ptr_width=32 object with symbols 0=o, 1=a, signatures o={"abi":"0.8","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[1],"kind":"oracle","mem":[],"tgt":1,"tier":"q"} and a={"abi":"0.8","args":["token"],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Exact LF-terminated functions:
oracle @o (x:wire in) (t:wire) (f:wire[4]) () ()
^entry():
lift.retval x
action @a (t:wire mut) () () (tk:token) ()
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
d = qalloc any 1
f = qalloc any 4
h c
oracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()
oracle_call @o tk (c) d f () ()
h c
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree f
qfree d
qfree c
Independent §9.2 interface=closure pins: o=cab76c914fa09a3fc8237381c6de91e83eeaefbd65cb7f52571ed4020abe8926; a=be1f0e087e06fecd99df7c3cbb5c3c8c186fde8f814be1f826487e858fa66296. Standard 0.8 header, canonical symbols line with these pins, blank section separator, functions above and final LF give object_hash=49ad3ba6c411ed73bebacdebe6728ebff5995dbf8bbc03c016d1cb0c5c3e8625. CLI hash and check both actually exit 1, empty stdout, “§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean”. Removing only the borrow/CX/return triplet makes parse/hash succeed. Hand: at token (1,0,0,0), each oracle XORs c into d and leaves f zero, so their pair is identity. At token (0,0,0,0), each XORs code 1 into f, which also cancels. Thus H;O;O;H is identity for every token, c=d=f=0 at the borrow, and CX(c,b) is identity on arbitrary b and any entangled reference. The opaque operation is not eligible for reversible(); sequence instead calls forget_inverses on all its operands, permanently deleting the initial H record. This requires no function-specific certificate: the oracle involution is normative.
codex.fix: In src/borrow.rs::Facts::sequence and the inverse-event representation, preserve a causal record for opaque XOR oracle applications and cancel a fully matched involution only when it tops all input/control/output histories. Include callee, token/classical specialization, effective controls and operand identities in matching; keep unmatched opaque readers as barriers to outer restoration. §5.2 explicitly says “The oracle is an involution on (ins, tgt, fr) and its own adjoint”; §5.3 says “oracle_call ↦ oracle_call” and “reverse order, instruction replaced, versions renumbered”; §6.2 says “other values are released only by the adjoint of the sequence that produced them”. These determine c=d=f=0 after the pair and final I_t ⊗ I_bR. Add r9_matched_opaque_oracle_restores_outer_fact to tests/r1_borrow.rs and a pinned tests/cli_xam.rs counterpart using the exact object above. Current Object::parse/check success assertions fail; after repair hash/check succeed with those pins, run-action a --arg token:1,0,0,0 --mut 0/1 preserves the corresponding basis state, and --state "0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8" is unchanged. Also test token:0,0,0,0, independently initialized --adjoint, wires=1, reverse equals_entry=true and a library-supplied borrowed wire Bell-paired with an untouched reference. Include a changed-input/unmatched-reader negative and a matched pair split across qloop 1 bodies; no new budget cap or certificate requirement.

codex.problem:
A nonzero mixed loop reuses physical names compiled for its first visit instead of threading reallocated bindings into subsequent visits. Memoryless ptr_width=32 sole symbol 0=a, signature {"abi":"0.8","args":[],"bounds":[2],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}. Exact LF-terminated function:
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
regs {  } bounds {2}
^entry():
c = qalloc any 1
qloop 2 {
b = qborrow any 1
cx c b
qreturn b
qfree c
c = qalloc any 1
h t
h t
}
qfree c
Independent interface=closure H=bb983f1dc5a8eea46912ea64d1226a9345a05d6cba6cc8452efc9f39b4a17a89; standard header/canonical stored-H symbols/functions object_hash=80478acc73d52bbf64c395816470293b5b4b4a1ee36a5c550bf00436f06fc192. Actual hash/check and run-action (t=0, independently adjoint t=1, and complex superposition) exit 1 with empty stdout and “§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean”. Count 1 succeeds; count 3 also fails. Expanding the two visits into consecutive source bodies, deleting bounds, passes check and all three executions, preserving t with one surviving wire. Hand: c starts clean; every visit borrows b, applies disabled CX(0,b), returns b unchanged, frees clean c, creates a new clean c, and applies H²=I to t. Every return is individually valid, including for externally entangled b; all workspace is clean at exit. Compiler::compile compiles the loop body once: the read/free of c names the pre-loop wire while the allocation publishes a different wire. Facts::repeat replays those fixed nodes; the second visit reads/frees the dead pre-loop wire instead of the current clean allocation.
codex.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile’s qloop lowering and the structured transfer representation so each executed visit resolves reads/releases against that visit’s entry binding map and publishes its successor bindings. Reuse an alpha-renamed or binding-parameterized transfer/cycle when environments recur, rather than unrolling huge counts or imposing a trip cap. Preserve zero-trip omission and lexical qregion hoisting. §4.6 defines qloop as “body n times”; §4.3 defines qalloc as “n clean wires” and qfree as “release a qallocated bundle clean on every basis configuration” (the spec spells qallocated as `qalloc`ed); §3.3 says “a name is not used after consume”; §5.3 requires adjoints with “versions renumbered”. Expected result is identity on t and each independently borrowed bR, with c=0 at every iteration entry and all releases. Add r9_mixed_loop_threads_reallocated_bindings to tests/r1_borrow.rs and tests/cli_xam.rs using the exact function/signature/hashes above. Current parse-success assertion fails; after repair parse/hash/check must succeed, run-action --mut 0/1 yields {"0":[1,0]}/{"1":[1,0]}, and --state "0=0.6,0;1=0,0.8" remains unchanged, independently forward and adjoint. Assert wires=1 and reverse equals_entry=true. Supply arbitrary/Bell-entangled borrowed entries in library tests. Include counts 0/1/2/3, nested loops, alpha-renamed straight-line expansion, and a dirty-control variant that still rejects at its first invalid return. No token or execution budget is needed.
